channel.title: In Palestine Today
channel.description: One day in Palestine, told in order, in Palestine’s time. Every figure and every accusation sourced.

item.title: Algeria, Kuwait and Arab Parliament join condemnation of Colombia’s Jerusalem embassy
item.description: Algeria said the step undermines the two-state solution; Kuwait urged the Security Council to act; the Arab Parliament’s speaker called it null and void. Source: WAFA (Algerian and Kuwaiti foreign ministries, Arab Parliament).

item.title: WAFA’s daily round-up: four killed in Gaza, dozens detained in West Bank
item.description: The agency’s closing tally lists raids, arrests, settler attacks, demolitions and road closures in the West Bank, and strikes and demolitions across Gaza. Source: WAFA (daily round-up).

item.title: Israeli forces raid Azzun and Tulkarm’s Shweikeh suburb, firing tear gas
item.description: Troops stopped cars and held passengers in Shweikeh and fired sound and gas grenades in Azzun; a checkpoint at Qalqilya’s southern entrance slowed traffic earlier. Source: WAFA.

item.title: UN says it recorded Israeli air strikes, shelling and gunfire across all of Gaza
item.description: Deputy spokesperson Farhan Haq said the aid the UN can bring in falls short of needs and that access is restricted to more than 64% of Gaza’s land. Source: WAFA (UN noon briefing).

item.title: Jordan and Australia reaffirm two-state solution, reject West Bank annexation
item.description: A joint statement after King Abdullah II’s talks with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Canberra also condemned the E1 settlement project as illegal. Source: WAFA (Jordan-Australia joint statement).

item.title: Journalists’ syndicate says Israel is waging a wide war on Palestinian reporters
item.description: The syndicate said 260 journalists have been killed in Gaza and more than 240 detained, 38 of whom are still held, and asked for protection in the field. Source: WAFA / Palestinian Journalists Syndicate.

item.title: Commission records 21 attacks on olive harvest across seven governorates in one day
item.description: Settlers carried out 12, the army 8 and one was joint, between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m., the Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said. Source: WAFA / Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission.

item.title: Three killed in Israeli strikes and fire in Gaza, bringing day’s toll to five, WAFA says
item.description: A drone strike on a car in al-Qarara, north of Khan Younis, killed two men and wounded a woman; another man was killed by gunfire in Jabalia camp. Source: WAFA.

item.title: Settlers attack Qawawis homes in Masafer Yatta; elderly man hurt, owner arrested
item.description: Settlers smashed doors and cameras before Israeli forces arrived and detained the owner of the damaged house; olives were stolen east of Yatta, an activist said. Source: WAFA.

item.title: Vice President al-Sheikh condemns Colombia’s embassy opening in Jerusalem
item.description: Hussein al-Sheikh said the move flouts international law and the city’s special legal and historical status, and urged the world to act. Source: WAFA.

item.title: Settlers beat three Palestinians in Abu Nujeim, southeast of Bethlehem, WAFA reports
item.description: One of the men was taken to hospital; the area has faced repeated attacks, including gunfire at residents’ cars in August, WAFA said. Source: WAFA.

item.title: Ministry condemns Mukhmas mosque arson as commission counts 23 since 2023
item.description: Racist slogans were sprayed on the Sultan Ibrahim Mosque, the ministry said; the commission counts 13 arson attacks on mosques so far in 2026. Source: WAFA / Palestinian Foreign Ministry; Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission.

item.title: Arab League, OIC and Egypt condemn Colombia’s Jerusalem embassy
item.description: The League cited Security Council resolutions 478 and 2334; the OIC chief wrote to Colombia’s foreign minister urging a reversal and warned of consequences. Source: WAFA (Arab League, OIC, Egyptian Foreign Ministry statements).

item.title: Israeli troops raid Red Crescent office and hospital in Salfit, seize camera footage
item.description: Soldiers threatened to open fire if the Yasser Arafat Hospital did not hand over its recordings, official sources told WAFA; troops came back later in the day. Source: WAFA (official sources).

item.title: Israel’s army chief warns of ‘potential for escalation,’ condemns settler violence
item.description: Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir said the army would keep enabling the olive harvest; the 98th Division has been sent to the West Bank, The Times of Israel reported. Source: The Times of Israel.

item.title: Arab League to mark its first remembrance day for what it calls genocide victims
item.description: Arab ministers designated 17 October each year; the League says more than 700 people were killed in Gaza on that day in 2023, including at al-Ahli hospital. Source: WAFA / Arab League.

item.title: PLO refugee official warns UNRWA against laying off staff over budget gap
item.description: Ahmad Abu Holi wrote to Commissioner-General Christian Saunders after Saunders said in Berlin that large layoffs were possible without new funding. Source: WAFA / PLO Department of Refugee Affairs.

item.title: Palestinian central bank chief urges IMF-backed fix for banking ties with Israel
item.description: Yahya Shunnar said about 50 billion shekels a year flows through correspondent banking with Israeli banks, whose legal cover has been cut to two-week periods. Source: WAFA / Palestine Monetary Authority.

item.title: Displaced families living in a Khan Younis cemetery patch tents before winter
item.description: A WAFA video shows families covering worn tents with nylon and tarpaulins against the rain, with no safe shelter as the wet season nears. Source: WAFA (video report).

item.title: Traders return to Khan Younis’s historic grain market
item.description: A WAFA video shows vendors back at work in the old market in southern Gaza as prices in the Strip keep climbing. Source: WAFA (video report).

item.title: Man, 90, and woman beaten during hours-long Israeli raid on Tammun, Red Crescent says
item.description: Special forces surrounded a house in the town south of Tubas; a young man was detained to pressure his brother to surrender, the Prisoners’ Society said. Source: WAFA / Palestine Red Crescent Society.

item.title: Israeli forces detain mother of man they killed in 2023, near Tulkarm checkpoint
item.description: The 47-year-old woman from Tulkarm refugee camp was detained near Jubara checkpoint, the Prisoners’ Society said; two young men were also arrested in the governorate. Source: WAFA / Palestinian Prisoners' Society.

item.title: Israeli forces ransack prisoners’ commission office in Salfit, demolish Haris workshops
item.description: Troops tore photographs and questioned staff at the office, its director said; three vehicle-repair shops owned by two brothers were razed in Haris. Source: WAFA.

item.title: More than 2,000 children detained since October 2023, Prisoners’ Society says
item.description: At least 350 remain in custody, the society said, after at least six children were detained overnight in Sa’ir and al-Shuyukh, near Hebron. Source: Quds News Network / Palestinian Prisoners' Society.

item.title: Colombia opens embassy in Jerusalem; Palestinian ministry calls it a violation
item.description: Colombia is the tenth country with an embassy in the city, Reuters reported; Ramallah says the move breaches Security Council resolutions 476 and 478. Source: WAFA (Palestinian Foreign Ministry); Reuters.

item.title: Tuqu’ sealed for a second day as Israeli forces install new gate near Jenin
item.description: All seven entrances to Tuqu’ are closed with iron gates, its mayor said; a new gate at Wad Da’uq follows gates fitted at Arraba’s entrances on Tuesday. Source: WAFA / Tuqu' Municipality.

item.title: Gaza health ministry says 68 of 116 hospital generators are out of service
item.description: Neonatal care at al-Rantisi and al-Shifa has been disrupted; a medical relief director says 2,027 patients have died awaiting treatment or evacuation. Source: Quds News Network / WAFA.

item.title: Egyptian surgeons resume open-heart operations at Gaza City hospital
item.description: The team at al-Quds Hospital, working with HEAL Palestine, aims to operate on about 30 patients while more than 200 critical cases wait, WAFA reported. Source: WAFA (video report).

item.title: Two women held in Damon prison have scabies, prisoners’ commission says
item.description: The detainees, aged 20 and 31, told a commission lawyer their rooms were raided with gas and sound grenades on 7 October and that food is scarce. Source: WAFA / Commission of Detainees' and Ex-Detainees' Affairs.

item.title: More than 430 Jerusalem homes and structures demolished this year, researcher says
item.description: Fakhri Abu Diab told Voice of Palestine radio that 23,280 demolition orders are in force and that no more than 1% of Jerusalemites who applied this year got permits. Source: WAFA.

item.title: Israeli bulldozers uproot hundreds of olive trees in Kafr Malik, sources say
item.description: Thirty-five dunums of farmland beside the bypass road were razed under a military order issued ten days earlier, local sources told WAFA. Source: WAFA.

item.title: Gaza death toll since October 2023 reaches 74,392, medical sources say
item.description: Three bodies and 17 injured people reached hospitals in 24 hours; 1,501 people have been killed since the ceasefire began a year ago. Source: WAFA / Gaza medical sources.

item.title: Amnesty Germany gives 2026 human rights award to children’s lawyer Khaled Quzmar
item.description: The Ramallah-based lawyer has defended Palestinian children for nearly 40 years; the prize will be presented in Berlin on 25 November, WAFA reported. Source: Amnesty International Germany / WAFA.

item.title: Settlers beat 17-year-old picking olives in Beita, Red Crescent says
item.description: In nearby Beit Furik, settlers stopped farmers harvesting east of al-Naqra road, in Area B, and dumped the olives they had gathered, local sources said. Source: WAFA / Palestine Red Crescent Society.

item.title: Settlers try to stop olive harvest in Turmus Ayya; residents push them back, sources say
item.description: The settlers retreated toward an outpost set up on the town’s plain late last year, local sources told WAFA. Source: WAFA.

item.title: Settlers bulldoze land in Beit Dajan and Burin to prepare new outpost, sources say
item.description: Two bulldozers opened new roads east of Beit Dajan and razed land around a family’s home in Burin, local and security sources told WAFA. Source: WAFA.

item.title: Israeli forces demolish home and family shelter in Masafer Yatta, sources say
item.description: An 80-square-metre house in Ighzaywa and a 40-square-metre shelter for a family of seven in Umm al-Khair were razed; a mobile toilet was seized. Source: WAFA.

item.title: Gaza consumer prices rose 11.36% in September, statistics bureau says
item.description: A 25-kilogram sack of white flour averaged 56 shekels in Gaza; prices rose 0.53% in the West Bank and 0.44% in Jerusalem, the bureau said. Source: WAFA / Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics.

item.title: Israeli forces detain a boy in Issawiya, Jerusalem Governorate says
item.description: Forces and Israeli municipal crews also entered the al-Bustan neighbourhood of Silwan, south of al-Aqsa Mosque, the governorate said. Source: WAFA / Jerusalem Governorate.

item.title: Troops tear-gas Jenin-area olive pickers despite prior coordination, sources say
item.description: Farmers from al-Fandaqumiya, Jaba’ and Silat al-Dhahr were forced out; in Ya’bad, settlers stole harvested olives and expelled pickers, local sources said. Source: WAFA.
